title: Survey on AI Ethics: A Socio-technical Perspective

bias_targets.methodology: As a survey paper, it reviews methodologies from existing literature, such as applying group fairness metrics (demographic parity, equalized odds) and using crafted input texts that differ only in gender to analyze variations in language model outputs.

The survey discusses evaluating racial bias through counterfactual fairness testing (e.g., altering a sensitive attribute like race to see if outcomes change) and assessing disparate impact in systems like criminal recidivism prediction.

The paper reviews techniques for measuring religious stereotypes in foundation models by providing crafted input texts that differ only in religious demographic information and analyzing the resulting variations in the model's output.

The survey outlines fairness-enhancing pre-processing methods designed to evaluate and obfuscate the influence of sensitive attributes, such as nationality, from training data to prevent discriminatory predictions.
